DYK: The construction industry has the second-highest rate of suicide in the U.S., with 53.3 per 100,000 workers. Construction Suicide Prevention Week – September 9-13 #CSPW2024 raises awareness of this crisis and provides resources to save lives.

Our industry prioritizes physical safety, but we must also focus on mental well-being to prevent further tragedies. Join DynaTen Corporation in creating a culture to check in with each other and standing against the stigma of mental illness and working to prevent suicide.

DynaTen employees can access the Employee Assistance Program (EAP) through Comfort Systems USA, offering resources for employees and their families. Additionally, poker chips will be available for discreetly offering extra support to those in need.

If you or someone you know is struggling or in crisis, help is available. Call or text 988 or chat at 988lifeline.org to reach the 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline.

#DynaTen #CSPW2024 #CSUSA

Second Chances was founded in 2011 as Second Chances Transitional Living for Women operating through 2016 by providing women involved with the judicial system with substance use and mental health challenges a place to regain their families and sobriety in a safe and loving environment. Our founder, Sandra Fedinic, dedicated her retirement years and savings to opening and running this home but fell seriously ill after 5 successful years in operation and was forced to place the nonprofit in dormant status. In early 2023 we were excited to file a petition for revival which was approved on February 9, 2023. 

We are currently attempting to raise funds to get programs running and have appointed a new Board President, Lisa Jersey, to help lead us to new heights and to serve women in our community once again. Our focus remains on serving women in Northern Nevada but will expand to serve all transitional living homes in our area by offering training and support for those who serve some of our most vulnerable populations. We believe that by leveraging the strengths and generosity of local businesses, leaders and other non-profits we can work to establish meaningful change and lasting community support for underserved women and their families. 

Second Chances is excited to be re-established in Reno, NV and is eager to bring our knowledge, experience and services back to our community again.

So excited to be a part of this with Second Chances Nonprofit 💜I am SO LOOKING FORWARD to having ONE HUNDRED participating businesses for Nevada's Recovery Friendly Workplace Initiative, and we're so close! Three digits worth of businesses in Nevada willing to say "we want to help you, don't suffer in silence, please say something!" 

Too often people suffering with mental health concerns, substance/alcohol use disorder, and other recovery related challenges fear retaliation or negative judgements for speaking up, so they don't. The stigma surrounding recovery related issues is often felt as being worse than the disorder itself, and is a huge hurdle to overcome. 

By becoming a recovery friendly workplace, that hurdle gets significantly reduced for those working there, and for communities affected by that workplace. A recovery friendly workplace invites their employees to bring their struggles out of the shadows so they can be honest about what they're going through, and find support, community, and compassion. To feel seen. 

In their 2022 global impact study, the society for human resource management found that if a company culture was deemed as being "poor" a staggering 87% felt its because "They don't care about me" in the workplace. The importance of "care", the importance of being seen, CANNOT be overlooked.

If you'd like to show your employees their workplace cares, go to ForRecovery.org/workplace and click "Get Started" to start the conversation. 

#Recovery
#FoundationforRecovery
#RecoveryFriendlyWorkplace
#Nevada
#Nevadabusiness

3)Pipes that run against exterior walls that have little or no insulation.

When you reach the temperature pipe's freeze (20° F or below), exposed pipes in spaces like attics are vulnerable. ❄️ Here are some tips to prevent freezing pipes in your attic. 

1. Wrap The Pipes And Water Lines: Pipes in attics and crawl spaces are often exposed to cold air, making them susceptible to freezing. 
2. Insulate the Attic: Besides insulating your attic pipes, the best thing to do is insulate the entire attic. A frozen pipe in the attic can affect the entire water line throughout the house, so insulating the attic will go a long way toward keeping the home safe and warm.
3. Airseal The Attic: The cold air that passes through small gaps and holes in the walls causes the temperature to drop inside the home, which could potentially freeze indoor pipes. 
4. Keep The Heat On: If you plan to stay away from your house for an extended period during freezing weather, keep your heating system inside your home. 
5. Shut Off the Main Water Supply: Besides keeping the heat on, you should consider turning off the water supply when leaving the house for a long time in winter.

Our technicians are here to provide a FREE ESTIMATE and help you understand how adding insulation can make your energy bill less costly and keep your home more comfortable. Chat / Book Appointment Online: aircoservice.com #aircoservice #atticinsulation

Have you ever noticed the phrase “auxiliary heat” on your thermostat? This function of your HVAC system is intended to do two things: supplement your heat pump's capacity during extreme cold weather and/or provide emergency heat if your system fails. 

1️⃣ Auxiliary heat should be a temporary setting and automatically turn off once your home warms up. Check back in 30 minutes or so to see if it has turned off on its own.
2️⃣ Only turn your heat up two degrees at a time. Auxiliary heat can be triggered if your home is three degrees lower than your set temperature.
3️⃣ Do not turn on emergency heat unless it’s actually an emergency. Give auxiliary heat time to work its magic. Emergency heat requires a lot more energy and is more expensive.
4️⃣ Make sure your aux heat indicator turns off when the outside temperature reaches 40 degrees or higher. If it remains on, you may have a malfunction in your heat pump.

If you think your heat source needs immediate attention and you're not getting enough heat into your home, you can trust us. Call us today or visit aircoservice.com to schedule an appointment. #aircoservice #auxiliaryheat #homeowneradvice

Don’t let plumbing problems ruin your holiday cheer! Clogged sinks, backed-up toilets, and drain issues are all too common during this festive season. Here are five tips to keep your home plumbing in tip-top shape: 🎅🏼🎄

1️⃣ Mind the garbage disposal: Leftovers belong in the trash, not the drain. Your garbage disposal isn't a catch-all!
2️⃣ Keep grease out of the sink: Before washing pans, soak up grease with paper towels and toss them in the trash. Grease down the drain = bad news.
3️⃣ Flush smart: Only flush toilet paper—no wet wipes, hygiene products, or anything else that can clog pipes. 
4️⃣ Give showers a break: Space out showers by at least 10 minutes to prevent overworking your water heater. 
5️⃣ Dishwasher do’s and don’ts: Avoid running the dishwasher while using the sink to reduce stress on your system. 

If a plumbing problem pops up, Airco Service is here to help. Visit aircoservice.com for expert solutions, even during the holidays! #aircoservice #plumbingtips #homeownertips

Second Chances was founded in 2011 as Second Chances Transitional Living for Women operating through 2016 by providing women involved with the judicial system with substance use and mental health challenges a place to regain their families and sobriety in a safe and loving environment. Our founder, Sandra Fedinic, dedicated her retirement years and savings to opening and running this home but fell seriously ill after 5 successful years in operation and was forced to place the nonprofit in dormant status. In early 2023 we were excited to file a petition for revival which was approved on February 9, 2023. 

We are currently attempting to raise funds to get programs running and have appointed a new Board President, Lisa Jersey, to help lead us to new heights and to serve women in our community once again. Our focus remains on serving women in Northern Nevada but will expand to serve all transitional living homes in our area by offering training and support for those who serve some of our most vulnerable populations. We believe that by leveraging the strengths and generosity of local businesses, leaders and other non-profits we can work to establish meaningful change and lasting community support for underserved women and their families. 

Second Chances is excited to be re-established in Reno, NV and is eager to bring our knowledge, experience and services back to our community again.

So excited to be a part of this with Second Chances Nonprofit 💜I am SO LOOKING FORWARD to having ONE HUNDRED participating businesses for Nevada's Recovery Friendly Workplace Initiative, and we're so close! Three digits worth of businesses in Nevada willing to say "we want to help you, don't suffer in silence, please say something!" 

Too often people suffering with mental health concerns, substance/alcohol use disorder, and other recovery related challenges fear retaliation or negative judgements for speaking up, so they don't. The stigma surrounding recovery related issues is often felt as being worse than the disorder itself, and is a huge hurdle to overcome. 

By becoming a recovery friendly workplace, that hurdle gets significantly reduced for those working there, and for communities affected by that workplace. A recovery friendly workplace invites their employees to bring their struggles out of the shadows so they can be honest about what they're going through, and find support, community, and compassion. To feel seen. 

In their 2022 global impact study, the society for human resource management found that if a company culture was deemed as being "poor" a staggering 87% felt its because "They don't care about me" in the workplace. The importance of "care", the importance of being seen, CANNOT be overlooked.

If you'd like to show your employees their workplace cares, go to ForRecovery.org/workplace and click "Get Started" to start the conversation.

Nick credits the freedom Powers management gives him to do his job and the relationships he’s built over the years as key reasons for his success and gratitude. Nick, thank you for being an invaluable part of Powers!

Getting your HVAC system balanced by professionals helps ensure even airflow, keeps everyone comfortable, and can save you money.

Powers is one of only a few Arkansas companies with NEBB-certified professionals on staff, so we can test, adjust, and balance commercial HVAC systems.
 
For more information about our NEBB TAB service, visit https://lnkd.in/gKKsaH-7 or call 877-274-7127.

Second Chances was founded in 2011 as Second Chances Transitional Living for Women operating through 2016 by providing women involved with the judicial system with substance use and mental health challenges a place to regain their families and sobriety in a safe and loving environment. Our founder, Sandra Fedinic, dedicated her retirement years and savings to opening and running this home but fell seriously ill after 5 successful years in operation and was forced to place the nonprofit in dormant status. In early 2023 we were excited to file a petition for revival which was approved on February 9, 2023. 

We are currently attempting to raise funds to get programs running and have appointed a new Board President, Lisa Jersey, to help lead us to new heights and to serve women in our community once again. Our focus remains on serving women in Northern Nevada but will expand to serve all transitional living homes in our area by offering training and support for those who serve some of our most vulnerable populations. We believe that by leveraging the strengths and generosity of local businesses, leaders and other non-profits we can work to establish meaningful change and lasting community support for underserved women and their families. 

Second Chances is excited to be re-established in Reno, NV and is eager to bring our knowledge, experience and services back to our community again.

So excited to be a part of this with Second Chances Nonprofit 💜I am SO LOOKING FORWARD to having ONE HUNDRED participating businesses for Nevada's Recovery Friendly Workplace Initiative, and we're so close! Three digits worth of businesses in Nevada willing to say "we want to help you, don't suffer in silence, please say something!" 

Too often people suffering with mental health concerns, substance/alcohol use disorder, and other recovery related challenges fear retaliation or negative judgements for speaking up, so they don't. The stigma surrounding recovery related issues is often felt as being worse than the disorder itself, and is a huge hurdle to overcome. 

By becoming a recovery friendly workplace, that hurdle gets significantly reduced for those working there, and for communities affected by that workplace. A recovery friendly workplace invites their employees to bring their struggles out of the shadows so they can be honest about what they're going through, and find support, community, and compassion. To feel seen. 

In their 2022 global impact study, the society for human resource management found that if a company culture was deemed as being "poor" a staggering 87% felt its because "They don't care about me" in the workplace. The importance of "care", the importance of being seen, CANNOT be overlooked.

If you'd like to show your employees their workplace cares, go to ForRecovery.org/workplace and click "Get Started" to start the conversation.

We are currently attempting to raise funds to get programs running and have appointed a new Board President, Lisa Jersey, to help lead us to new heights and to serve women in our community once again. Our focus remains on serving women in Northern Nevada but will expand to serve all transitional living homes in our area by offering training and support for those who serve some of our most vulnerable populations. We believe that by leveraging the strengths and generosity of local businesses, leaders and other non-profits we can work to establish meaningful change and lasting community support for underserved women and their families. 

Second Chances is excited to be re-established in Reno, NV and is eager to bring our knowledge, experience and services back to our community again.

Second Chances was founded in 2011 as Second Chances Transitional Living for Women operating through 2016 by providing women involved with the judicial system with substance use and mental health challenges a place to regain their families and sobriety in a safe and loving environment. Our founder, Sandra Fedinic, dedicated her retirement years and savings to opening and running this home but fell seriously ill after 5 successful years in operation and was forced to place the nonprofit in dormant status. In early 2023 we were excited to file a petition for revival which was approved on February 9, 2023. 

We are currently attempting to raise funds to get programs running and have appointed a new Board President, Lisa Jersey, to help lead us to new heights and to serve women in our community once again. Our focus remains on serving women in Northern Nevada but will expand to serve all transitional living homes in our area by offering training and support for those who serve some of our most vulnerable populations. We believe that by leveraging the strengths and generosity of local businesses, leaders and other non-profits we can work to establish meaningful change and lasting community support for underserved women and their families. 

Second Chances is excited to be re-established in Reno, NV and is eager to bring our knowledge, experience and services back to our community again.

Vanwege de fijne samenwerking tijdens 'project Phoenix' heeft United Rentals namens EQIN en Indu-Tools alle medewerkers en contractors van AVR Rozenburg afgelopen week getrakteerd op friet en snacks!

Deze traktatie was een blijk van waardering en als extra steuntje in de rug voor iedereen die zich dag en nacht inzet om de werkzaamheden veilig en op tijd af te ronden. We zijn trots op ons Phoenix-teamen alle partners die samen de schouders eronder zetten. Stay tuned voor meer updates en ontwikkelingen. Samen bouwen we aan een duurzame toekomst! 🌍

We're thrilled to introduce our new President and CEO, Mike Blakeley, to everyone allied with BBB® across the San Francisco Bay Area and Northern Coastal California!  Blakeley succeeds Lori Wilson, who is retiring after 35 long, service-filled years. We can't thank Lori enough for her dedication! 

With over 20 years of experience, Blakeley is a strategic leader who has driven economic development, policy innovation, and organizational transformation across corporate, nonprofit, and global consulting sectors. Blakeley was previously CEO of the Marin Economic Forum where he led the creation of Marin County’s first-ever economic strategy through a landmark public-private partnership.

The BBB Board of Directors conducted a national search in partnership with Cook Silverman Search, ensuring a thorough and inclusive process.

For more information about the Better Business Bureau, visit www.BBB.org.

Don't let the cold weather put your plumbing at risk! Pipes that freeze most frequently are:

1) Pipes exposed to severe cold, like outdoor hose bibs, swimming pool supply lines, and water sprinkler lines.
2) Water supply pipes in unheated interior areas like basements, crawl spaces, attics, garages, or kitchen cabinets.
3)Pipes that run against exterior walls that have little or no insulation.

When you reach the temperature pipe's freeze (20° F or below), exposed pipes in spaces like attics are vulnerable. ❄️ Here are some tips to prevent freezing pipes in your attic. 

1. Wrap The Pipes And Water Lines: Pipes in attics and crawl spaces are often exposed to cold air, making them susceptible to freezing. 
2. Insulate the Attic: Besides insulating your attic pipes, the best thing to do is insulate the entire attic. A frozen pipe in the attic can affect the entire water line throughout the house, so insulating the attic will go a long way toward keeping the home safe and warm.
3. Airseal The Attic: The cold air that passes through small gaps and holes in the walls causes the temperature to drop inside the home, which could potentially freeze indoor pipes. 
4. Keep The Heat On: If you plan to stay away from your house for an extended period during freezing weather, keep your heating system inside your home. 
5. Shut Off the Main Water Supply: Besides keeping the heat on, you should consider turning off the water supply when leaving the house for a long time in winter.

Our technicians are here to provide a FREE ESTIMATE and help you understand how adding insulation can make your energy bill less costly and keep your home more comfortable. Chat / Book Appointment Online: aircoservice.com #aircoservice #atticinsulation

Have you ever noticed the phrase “auxiliary heat” on your thermostat? This function of your HVAC system is intended to do two things: supplement your heat pump's capacity during extreme cold weather and/or provide emergency heat if your system fails. 

1️⃣ Auxiliary heat should be a temporary setting and automatically turn off once your home warms up. Check back in 30 minutes or so to see if it has turned off on its own.
2️⃣ Only turn your heat up two degrees at a time. Auxiliary heat can be triggered if your home is three degrees lower than your set temperature.
3️⃣ Do not turn on emergency heat unless it’s actually an emergency. Give auxiliary heat time to work its magic. Emergency heat requires a lot more energy and is more expensive.
4️⃣ Make sure your aux heat indicator turns off when the outside temperature reaches 40 degrees or higher. If it remains on, you may have a malfunction in your heat pump.

If you think your heat source needs immediate attention and you're not getting enough heat into your home, you can trust us. Call us today or visit aircoservice.com to schedule an appointment. #aircoservice #auxiliaryheat #homeowneradvice

Don’t let plumbing problems ruin your holiday cheer! Clogged sinks, backed-up toilets, and drain issues are all too common during this festive season. Here are five tips to keep your home plumbing in tip-top shape: 🎅🏼🎄

1️⃣ Mind the garbage disposal: Leftovers belong in the trash, not the drain. Your garbage disposal isn't a catch-all!
2️⃣ Keep grease out of the sink: Before washing pans, soak up grease with paper towels and toss them in the trash. Grease down the drain = bad news.
3️⃣ Flush smart: Only flush toilet paper—no wet wipes, hygiene products, or anything else that can clog pipes. 
4️⃣ Give showers a break: Space out showers by at least 10 minutes to prevent overworking your water heater. 
5️⃣ Dishwasher do’s and don’ts: Avoid running the dishwasher while using the sink to reduce stress on your system. 

If a plumbing problem pops up, Airco Service is here to help. Visit aircoservice.com for expert solutions, even during the holidays! #aircoservice #plumbingtips #homeownertips
